items.text: Oil prices (WTI -4.4% week-on-week to $89.62, Brent -5.9% to $92.14) have retreated sharply, easing inflationary pressure from the upstream. However, the ECB explicitly flagged energy shocks as an ongoing upside inflation risk and downside growth risk as of late October; this remains a monitor for credit quality in cyclical sectors and spillovers to USD-funded sovereigns exposed to energy.

Headline CPI (3.72% YoY as of Sep) and core PCE (3.12% YoY) remain sticky above 2.5% target despite PPI moderating month-over-month. UMich 1-year inflation expectations fell sharply to 4.3% (from 4.7%), a signal the market is slowly pricing in rate cuts; watch whether October–November CPI and PCE soften enough to unlock Fed pivot narrative that could compress credit spreads.

Unemployment 4.1% (Oct), jobless claims recently at 200k (Nov 7), and AHE growth at 3.12% YoY suggest labor markets remain solid but cooling. Payrolls in October jumped to 165k (from 60k prior month), a likely seasonal outlier. The trend is moderation without collapse—tight enough to sustain services expansion (ISM Services 54.5 in October) but loose enough to avoid wage-price spiral.

UST 10y jumped 29bp to 5.15%, 2y at 4.88%, steepening the curve (10-2 spread 29bp). Fed funds held at 4.0%. ECB deposit rate at 2.50%, holding after October hold; Dec 17 meeting is 94% priced for a hike. Rates complexity: curve steepening on stronger growth (GDP 3.4% in Q2, GDPNow 3.48%), but IG credit spreads have compressed and CCC spreads are only 1316bp—tight for the refinancing wall ahead.

IG OAS 89bp and HY OAS 323bp show compressed risk premiums despite elevated base rates and mixed economic signals. CCC tightest at 1316bp, a red flag for covenant-lite issuers and legacy LBO debt rolling into a higher-for-longer regime. VIX at 19.3 (down from 25.6) suggests complacency; watch for sector-specific dislocations, especially in real estate and autos where refinancing pressure is real.

October retail sales posted 13th consecutive month of gains (+0.15% m/m, +3.57% YoY via NRF), but the monthly pace was slowest in a year—a signal that high gas prices and rate pressure are testing discretionary budgets. Existing home sales dropped to 3.75M (Oct) from 3.97M; mortgage rates at 7.11% are still elevation. Saving rate at 3.8% (Sep) has compressed, limiting consumer resilience.

China's official manufacturing PMI at 49.3 (Oct), slipping back into contraction after one month above 50; Caixin (private) also cooled. This matters: a China hard landing scenario (coupled with US credit overleverage) could trigger a commodities and EM credit shock, with ripple effects into US corporate earnings and high-yield default rates. Monitor this as the market's biggest latent tail risk.

themeCards.title: Rates Steepening into Refinancing Wall
themeCards.statusLine: 10y jumped 29bp to 5.15%, curve steepens to 29bp, while Fed holds at 4.0%. Base rates remain punitive for 2026–2027 refinancing maturities, especially in mid-market and CCC.
themeCards.relevance: Credit investors face a wall of near-term maturities rolling into a higher-for-longer regime. IG spreads at 89bp and HY at 323bp leave minimal cushion if earnings disappoint or credit events surface in cyclical sectors.

themeCards.title: China Demand Cliff & Commodity Shock
themeCards.statusLine: Official NBS PMI dropped to 49.3 (Oct), signaling renewed contraction and weak demand signals rippling through export orders. Domestic stimulus has not yet reignited growth.
themeCards.relevance: A sustained China downturn threatens US corporate earnings leverage in cyclicals and EM sovereigns, while commodity volatility (oil already -5%) risks broader credit stress. Special-situations investors should monitor distressed issuers with China/commodity exposure.

themeCards.title: CCC Covenant-Lite Refinancing Crunch
themeCards.statusLine: CCC spreads at 1316bp—the tightest in the capital structure—despite rising default risks in legacy LBO cohorts. 2026–2027 maturities are significant, and many cov-lite borrowers lack cushion for earnings misses.
themeCards.relevance: Distressed debt opportunities: potential covenant breaches, extension negotiations, and opportunistic pickup in names facing refinancing gates before sentiment turns. Watch for first signs of maturity extensions or credit event announcements.

themeCards.title: Commercial Real Estate Stressed Credit
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales down to 3.75M (Oct), mortgage rates at 7.11%, and commercial cap rates under pressure. Office/hospitality refinancing risk remains acute as cap-rate compression reverses.
themeCards.relevance: Dislocations in CRE-linked mezzanine debt, CMBS, and leveraged landlord debt are ongoing. Special-situations teams should focus on trading impaired pools and sponsorship changes in distressed CRE portfolios.

themeCards.title: Persistent Inflation Stickiness & Rate Expectations
themeCards.statusLine: Core PCE at 3.12%, core CPI at 2.57%, and both sticky despite moderating energy. UMich 1-year expectations fell to 4.3%, hinting at peak-rate expectations, but Fed pivot window is still narrow.
themeCards.relevance: If inflation re-accelerates (or expectations reset higher), rates could spike further, forcing wider credit spreads and stress on duration-heavy portfolios. Conversely, if inflation fades, low-quality issuers gain breathing room. Inflation expectations are the key cross-asset macro signal.

regime.label: Late-cycle with tail risks
regime.detail: Rates elevated and sticky, labor cooling but holding, credit spreads compressed, China weakening, refinancing wall approaching.
